items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I says, 'I'm Buddy Tate, Mr. Armstrong, I'd like to meet you.' He says, 'Yeah, Pops.' He shook my hand.

ctx.x: First of all, you were going to tell me about meeting Louie.

Oh, yeah. Well, you remember I mentioned the small hotel where I first -- I mean, where I first heard Lester playing the tenor, the switch, you know, this is a small hotel where everybody used to go down in the lobby and jam, had a baby grand piano down there. So I was playing with this same T. Holder band and Louie played a one-nighter there -- had a big band during -- I think it was about 1931. Might have been '31. Anyway, -- and he was sitting out there -- we stayed there -- and he was sitting out in the…

him and I told him that -- I says, "I sure would like to come to New York some day." "You'll make it." He says, "You'll make it." He says, -- I say, "Yeah, but everybody in New York -- I'm afraid of New York." He said, "Man, there's a lot of cats in New York can't play, you know."
